summary: Validated (validate --run <run> --submission update31.json → valid=true). New finding continuing the guard-asymmetry pattern: the heartbeat fast path is the only RPC admission route that does not apply the shared protocol-version check. The general handler validates the header against the supported window and rejects out-of-window messages before dispatching (raft.go:1390-1394, 43-67); the heartbeat handler checks only that the instance is running and that the envelope carries an AppendEntries request, then calls the same append-entries logic (1415-1436). Because a heartbeat's field pattern is empty, what it can change is bounded to the term, the leader record, the contact refresh and the response — so a peer more than one version behind keeps its heartbeats honoured (higher term adopted, recorded as leader, contact kept fresh) while every entry-bearing message from that peer is refused before dispatch. The follower is then pinned to a leader it cannot replicate from and never starts an election because its contact keeps being refreshed: a deterministic stall, gated by a version mix the library documents as unsupported (support extends one version back), which is how I bounded the severity honestly in the record. A second observation from the same pair of functions is documentary: the handler's comment says it must only be called from the main thread, contradicting both the registration comment requiring it to be safe concurrently with a blocking RPC and the transport that invokes it on a connection goroutine — the earlier record established that the real safety comes from the transport restricting the fast path to zero-field heartbeats, so this is a misleading comment rather than evidence of a race. Recorded as one Fact plus an 'explained' interpretation with a discriminator (a receiver at the current protocol version with an older peer acting as leader), and counterevidence preserved: staying within the documented version range never reaches the scenario, no entries can be injected through the fast path, the affected node still answers heartbeats and is observable, and nothing was executed at runtime.
